title: Querying a database with SQL
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Query desk
objectives: know how SELECT and FROM choose the fields and the table a query reads
understand how WHERE decides which records a query hands back
know how to join conditions with AND and OR, and how to sort results with ORDER BY
starter: A table called Tree holds the fields Name, Height and Native, and 30 records. Write down how many fields and how many records come back from SELECT Name, Height FROM Tree, and which clause you would add to cut the records down.

stations.name: SELECT and FROM
stations.fact: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, and it is a language for asking rather than for programming.
stations.challenge: Which part of a query decides how many records come back?

stations.name: WHERE
stations.fact: WHERE looks at each record on its own and decides whether to keep it or drop it.
stations.challenge: Which records come back from a query that has no WHERE at all?

stations.name: Comparing values
stations.fact: SQL writes 'not equal to' as <>, where Python writes it as !=.

stations.name: AND and OR
stations.fact: AND narrows the results down and OR widens them out, which is worth saying out loud as you write.

stations.fact: Ascending is the default order, which SQL calls ASC, so it is almost never typed out.

keyq: Which clause of a query decides which fields come back, and which clause decides which records?
exam: A query is written SELECT Title FROM Game ORDER BY Length WHERE Players = 2. State the error in it, and write the query out corrected.
A table called Track holds the fields Title, Artist, Seconds and Genre. Write a query that lists the title and artist of every track longer than 240 seconds, longest first.
Using the same Track table, write a query that lists the title of every track that is Jazz or Blues and lasts under 180 seconds.
